title: Canonical homology and cohomology comparison over a geometric point
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $k$ a separably closed field, $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a scheme morphism, and $F$ an $A$-module sheaf on $X$. For integers $n,q$ with $2+n=q$, construct the canonical isomorphism $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,H^n(Ra_*(F[0][2])))\simeq H^q(X,F[0])$ [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The sections functor is exactly the inverse of the adopted constant-sheaf equivalence at the separably closed point. The isomorphism is the composite of the specified shift, exact-sections/homology and derived-global-sections/direct-image comparisons.

source.place: Geometric-fibre Kummer-class calculation and finite coefficient extension

proof.text: This is an explicit construction, with no chosen existence witness. Commute derived direct image with the shift by two, then use the homology shift comparison for 2+n=q. Sections on the separably closed point are exact, so mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso identifies sections of Hq with Hq of derived sections. The adopted rightDerivedGlobalSectionsIsoOfIsSepClosed identifies those derived sections with the canonical derived global-sections functor. Finally compose with rightDerivedLowerStarCompRightDerivedGlobalSectionsIso. The resulting actual composite is the stated isomorphism. No properness or connectedness of X is needed.

def ordinaryFinitePushforward_single_shift_homology_iso
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (n q : ℤ) (hq : 2 + n = q) :
    (constantSheafEquivalenceOfIsSepClosed A (k := k)).inverse.obj
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
        ((ordinaryFinitePushforward A a).obj
          (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧))) ≅
    (cohomology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X q).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)
